column3: The automations row imports the session-scoped xin.schedules document at boot: each record becomes automation sched-<id> (DAILY/WEEKLY/HOURLY with INTERVAL=1 and BYDAY/BYHOUR/BYMINUTE becomes a 5-field cron in the record tz, missing BYHOUR/BYMINUTE/BYDAY taken from the anchor as the old rule did; a future at becomes a once trigger; COUNT, UNTIL, INTERVAL>1, MONTHLY or a future DTSTART import disabled with no trigger and the original RRULE appended to the prompt). this_session and a reserved new_once keep their conversation as a same-thread target, new becomes fresh in the origin conversation's project, active becomes enabled. A slot due and not delivered per the record cursor (an at that never ran, a deploy mid-send, a slot missed while the home slept) is queued once as run legacy:<id>:<slot> before the automation is created, so create's arm fires it at the next wake. Then the document is retired in its own commit
column4: review finding (High): the PR dropped every existing schedule on upgrade. Queuing the run with store.addRun instead of engine.trigger avoids dispatching thread.create during plugin apply; the derived automation and run ids make a boot that crashed before the retire repeat the import without duplicates. A failed import is logged and keeps the document for the next boot instead of failing the plugin
column6: adopted; an unmappable schedule that was mid-send is not re-run because its due slot cannot be computed without the old RRULE engine
